REASONING:
Step 1 – Frame the project  
- Objective: improve tourism infrastructure and services, upgrade natural and cultural heritage sites, boost sustainable tourism in the Arequipa‑Colca corridor.  
- Scope: Four components (tourism attractions, roads + water/sanitation/health, institutional strengthening, PIU); 33 sub‑projects.  
- Delivery model: Regional Government of Arequipa (GORE) implements through a newly created Project Implementation Unit (PIU); oversight by MINCETUR, MEF and high‑level steering/consultative committees; inter‑institutional agreements with municipalities and stakeholders.  
- Timeline: Expected approval 09‑Jul‑2026, closing 30‑Jun‑2032; key milestones – PIU staff hired within 60 days, stakeholder‑engagement plan in 90 days, capacity‑building plan in 120 days; infrastructure works expected to be completed by 2031.  
- Budget: Total cost US$97.8 m (WB financing US$77.2 m). Component costs: $51.17 m, $37.06 m, $3.46 m, $5.91 m.  
- Key stakeholders: Republic of Peru (borrower), GORE Arequipa (implementing agency), MINCETUR (lead formulation), MEF, Ministry of Culture, MTC, Ministry of Health, SERNANP, local municipalities, indigenous groups, women’s associations, private investors, development partners (IFC, JICA, IDB, CAF, etc.).  
- External dependencies: Climate‑related hazards (floods, landslides, earthquakes, El Niño), private‑sector investment decisions, World Bank disbursement conditions, national accounting system (SIAF), procurement regulations.

Step 2 – Category sweep (candidate risks with supporting text)  
Technical: climate‑hazard damage to infrastructure (climate hazards … floods … mudslides … heavy rains destroy cultural sites); road‑safety risk (higher fatality rate, safety features required); earthquake damage to heritage churches (many having suffered earthquake damage).  
Financial: GORE’s inexperience with WB‑financed projects (capacity‑building required); delayed recruitment of FM staff; budget allocation/execution delays; potential accounting inaccuracies; unclear internal PIU coordination.  
Schedule: withdrawal condition needing three Interinstitutional Agreements could stall cash flow.  
Stakeholder: fragmented institutional coordination; need for Interinstitutional Agreements with municipalities; private‑sector investment conditional on upgrades; sexual exploitation/harassment risk for women; community resistance/FPIC.  
Political/Regulatory: recent political instability in Peru.  
External: market‑demand shock affecting economic returns (sensitivity analysis).  

Step 3 – Evidence filter  
All above risks are directly quoted in the appraisal document; no invented risks retained.

Step 4 – Assess & mitigate (likelihood 1‑5, impact 1‑5)  

| ID | Category | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation (concise) |
|----|----------|------------|--------|----------------------|
| R01 | environmental | 4 | 4 | Climate‑resilient designs, hazard mapping, insurance, emergency response plan. |
| R02 | technical | 3 | 3 | Apply strict road‑safety standards, guardrails, markings, pedestrian crossings; independent safety audits. |
| R03 | technical | 3 | 4 | Use seismic‑resistant construction, structural assessments, retrofit heritage sites. |
| R04 | financial | 3 | 4 | Targeted FM capacity‑building, appoint experienced FM specialist early, regular external audits. |
| R05 | financial | 2 | 3 | Prepare TORs early, fast‑track hiring, use interim staff if needed. |
| R06 | financial | 3 | 3 | Initiate budget allocation immediately, monthly execution monitoring, align with POM. |
| R07 | financial | 2 | 3 | Train staff on SIAF, implement double‑check controls, schedule annual independent audits. |
| R08 | organizational | 3 | 3 | Define PIU roles in POM, hold weekly coordination meetings, use RACI matrix. |
| R09 | schedule | 2 | 4 | Sign three Interinstitutional Agreements within first 90 days; assign dedicated liaison team. |
| R10 | stakeholder | 3 | 3 | Activate steering/consultative committees, joint work plan, formal MoUs. |
| R11 | stakeholder | 2 | 3 | Early stakeholder consultations, obtain FPIC where required, incorporate feedback. |
| R12 | external | 3 | 3 | Deliver key infrastructure on time, transparent investor communication, offer Obras por Impuestos incentives. |
| R13 | political_regulatory | 2 | 4 | Secure multi‑year regional/national commitments, embed in development plan, broad political advocacy. |
| R14 | external | 3 | 4 | Robust marketing plan, diversify products, monitor demand, adjust investments. |
| R15 | stakeholder | 2 | 3 | Zero‑tolerance SEA/SH policy, staff training, grievance mechanism, monitor complaints. |

Step 5 – Consolidate  
All identified risks have distinct evidence and are retained (15 risks). No duplicates remain.
